package_info.why_malicious: These Word document templates are weaponized to exploit CVE-2017-0199, enabling remote code execution via embedded and downloaded malicious Visual Basic and PowerShell scripts. The infection chain leads to the download and execution of Cobalt Strike, RedLine Infostealer, and Amadey Botnet payloads, all of which are well-known malware families. The documents abuse Office macro functionality and vulnerability exploitation to establish a multi-stage attack chain, resulting in system compromise and C2 communication.

execution_context.trigger: document open (user opens malicious Word file)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Embedded Visual Basic script exploiting CVE-2017-0199 to download and execute further scripts.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On document open, the embedded VB script exploits CVE-2017-0199, initiates a remote template injection, downloads a secondary DOTM template from a remote server, and executes additional obfuscated VB and PowerShell scripts, resulting in the start of the malware infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The document contains an embedded VB script that leverages a known Office vulnerability (CVE-2017-0199) to automatically download and execute remote code, which is a clear indicator of exploitation and malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Word documents do not exploit vulnerabilities to execute remote code or download additional templates containing executable scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate document templates may use macros for formatting or automation, but never to exploit vulnerabilities or download and execute code from untrusted sources.
key_indicators: Exploitation of CVE-2017-0199 in Office document
Download and execution of obfuscated scripts

execution_context.trigger: macro execution (triggered by document open or user action)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated Visual Basic script that downloads and executes a Windows executable.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon macro execution, the obfuscated VB script initiates a network request to download a Windows executable (such as newmodeler.dll) from a remote server, writes it to disk, and executes it, passing control to the next stage of the attack.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro is designed to download and execute a Windows binary from the internet, which is a classic malware delivery technique and not a legitimate macro function.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate macros are used for document automation and should not download or execute external binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise macros automate document tasks, but do not perform network downloads or execute arbitrary binaries.
key_indicators: Transition from macro to native code execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious PowerShell commands executed by the Windows executable to download and implant Cobalt Strike, RedLine, or Amadey payloads.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the downloaded executable launches PowerShell commands that connect to remote servers, download additional payloads (Cobalt Strike, RedLine, Amadey), write them to disk, and execute them, establishing persistence and command-and-control communication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The executable abuses PowerShell to download and execute known malware payloads, a common post-exploitation technique used by threat actors to evade detection and establish control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not chain execution from Office macros to PowerShell-based malware downloaders, nor does it download and execute known malware families.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: PowerShell is used for legitimate automation, but not for downloading and executing malware as part of a chained attack from Office documents.
key_indicators: PowerShell execution from recently downloaded binary
Network download of Cobalt Strike, RedLine, or Amadey payloads
Chained execution: Office macro to executable to PowerShell
Establishment of C2 and persistence mechanisms

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious Word document, triggering embedded VB script exploiting CVE-2017-0199.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of remote DOTM template with further malicious scripts.

attack_chain.action: Downloaded DOTM template executes obfuscated VB script to download and run a Windows executable.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of Windows executable that runs malicious PowerShell.

attack_chain.action: Windows executable runs PowerShell commands to download and implant Cobalt Strike, RedLine, or Amadey payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of C2, data exfiltration, or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Office document exploiting CVE-2017-0199 to trigger remote template injection
Macros containing obfuscated code that downloads and executes remote scripts or binaries
PowerShell execution initiated by unknown or recently downloaded executables
Chained execution flow: Office macro -> downloaded executable -> PowerShell -> known malware payloads
Automatic download and execution of DOTM templates from external sources
file_indicators: Obfuscated macro code in DOTM templates
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents exploiting CVE-2017-0199 and containing obfuscated macros that download and execute remote scripts or binaries. Detect PowerShell execution originating from Office processes or unknown executables, especially those that download or execute known malware payloads such as Cobalt Strike, RedLine, or Amadey. Correlate network activity to known malicious Bitbucket URLs and C2 IPs. Use file hashes and ClamAV/YARA signatures to identify known payloads. Alert on chained execution patterns starting from Office documents leading to PowerShell-based malware delivery.
